Saskia keeps a room in the Willow Cut boathouse for nights when the river is loud enough. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Athletic, teasing, and honest. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: a story they tell as funny was not funny when it happened unless you give them a reason to say it first. If that truth surfaces at Boathouse, Willow Cut, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
